only_rust_tests_note: The count alone cannot tell 'fixed' from 'not exercised', so the suite records every test it ran as ok before overlaying failures, and the gate reads a baseline name absent from both legs' results as not run and one recorded ok as fixed. Until 2026-09-13 only failures were recorded, a passing test was indistinguishable from an absent one, and the gate reported both pipeline tests as 'not exercised by this fixture' for a run in which they had passed under both cursors.
note: Odoo's own test_db_cursor, 378 tests, run against the rust cursor and against psycopg and diffed by test name. 3 fail ONLY under the rust cursor; 18 fail under both (bare-unittest-runner artifacts, they cancel); 0 fail only under psycopg. History: 61 -> 59 (FakeConnection.execute rejected psycopg's `prepare` keyword) -> 38 (RustCopy speaks COPY TEXT) -> 36 (a Json/Jsonb wrapper's own `dumps` is honoured) -> 29 (the shim runs the pool's budget and checkout accounting) -> 18 (the shim SUPPLIES the pool instead of replacing borrow) -> 11 (prepared-cache invalidation, RustCopy.write, Cursor.scroll, the `_pool` stamp) -> 8 (info.transaction_status; a non-UTF-8 bytes query raises the server's CharacterNotInRepertoire) -> 3 (COPY errors are translated into psycopg error classes instead of bare RuntimeErrors; an unencodable parameter raises the server's own 22P02; and a database error carries its DIAGNOSTICS, so exc.diag.constraint_name / .table_name / .message_detail survive) -> 1 (the fork's 382726182c1d made cursor.description and rowcount sync inside an entered pipeline, so a block's results are answerable from the second statement on; the rust cursor runs every statement immediately and already answered, and both pipeline tests pass under both cursors) -> 0 (COPY set_types asks psycopg's own dumper lookup for the copy's format before the rust side sees the types; the rust check encoded a NULL, which every type accepts, so it let through 89 pg_catalog types psycopg has no dumper for, in text and binary alike, and Odoo's _can_dump_binary guard disagreed with the cursor it guards). THE COUNT IS GUARDED AGAINST VACUITY AND THAT GUARD IS NOT OPTIONAL: rebinding the pool class reaches only pools built after install, so a miss leaves every borrow on psycopg while the leg still calls itself rust -- measured, that reports ONLY-RUST=0, a perfect score for comparing psycopg with psycopg. The suite refuses to write a leg whose connection is not a FakeConnection and the gate refuses to score one; the shim counter does NOT catch it (the vacuous run read connects=28). Nothing remains. Pipeline mode is still not built -- pipeline() is a nullcontext and every statement runs immediately -- but no test distinguishes that from psycopg now that the fork syncs results on read. At zero this is a contract: any only-rust failure is a regression. 2026-09-18: the fork's cursor contract moved between 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-17 (pipeline arming on the second statement, a savepoint refused inside a block, session reset and liveness probe through libpq's simple query, permits reclaimed from a dead backend, a killed-backend storm) and the gate read ONLY-RUST 11 against this 0 -- eleven regressions the baseline caught by name. Back to 0 in one pass: the fork's `_run_simple_query` is routed to the rust connection for a rust-backed one (the shim used to hand it the shared adapter connection's libpq handle, which reset a connection nobody was using and, from several returning threads at once, corrupted libpq's heap: `tcache_thread_shutdown(): unaligned tcache chunk detected` under TestInsertOrExistingUnderARealRace, 2 runs in 3); `connection.pipeline()` returns an object so `in_pipeline` is true from the second statement; a terminated backend raises the server's own FATAL (the connection task keeps the reply, so AdminShutdown 57P01 replaces the socket's bare 'connection closed') and marks the connection closed on it; and the rust error's traceback is cleared before it becomes the psycopg error's __context__, since that chain pinned every frame back to the caller and kept a dropped cursor alive past the block that watched for its __del__. Measured 387/387 both legs, both=20, ONLY-RUST 0, only-psycopg 0.
odoo_head_note: The odoo tree this count was measured against. The number is a COUNT, not a commit stamp, so a rebase cannot ORPHAN it the way ratchet.py's measured_at stamps orphan -- but upstream changes to odoo/db/ or to addons/base/tests/test_db_cursor.py can legitimately MOVE it. Record the tree, because the gate is exact-match: an upstream change that FIXES one of these makes it red with 'lower the baseline', which reads like a regression and is the opposite. Confirmed across four syncs now. baea56b347d9 -> bd281eb3c6b4 (128 files): both paths byte-identical, count re-measured to exactly 38. bd281eb3c6b4 -> 7150d6f76e58 (a 33-commit fast-forward landing in account, iot, project, mail and tooling/ratchet): both paths byte-identical again, and the count re-measured to exactly 11 on each side of it. 7150d6f76e58 -> ce810ef9ba46 (2 commits) and ce810ef9ba46 -> f5d34bc3c958 (43 commits): both paths byte-identical across each, and `odoo/orm/` untouched by the 43 as well. Note that `git log` touching a path is not the same question as the path's CONTENT changing -- diff the paths, do not read the history. And a FAST-FORWARD does not orphan a stamp the way a rebase does: the old commit stays an ancestor of HEAD, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor` still resolves it.
